column3: This process map covers phases commonly involved in a dispute resolution process the result of which is legally binding on the parties even if they don't agree. Examples are civil litigation, arbitration or expert determination (as opposed to non-binding processes such as negotiation, mediation or early neutral evaluation). The process map aims to be relevant across different types of process and national traditions so as to enable them to be handled and analysed in a like-for-like way. For instance, evidence and written submissions are covered in a single phase rather than separating them out in a system-specific way. More specific process maps are based on this parent one.

Covers exchange of information and positions before formal proceedings, initiation of formal proceedings, and exchange of initial claims and responses. Open statements of a party's legal position are included here; settlement proposals are excluded (see Settlement phase). Procedural failures at commencement (eg failure to pay filing fees, service issues) are included here; disputes about jurisdiction belong in Related proceedings.
